Core of the .NET convex decomposition packages (CuACD.NET, CoACD.NET, VHACD.NET): Mesh and IConvexDecomposer, plus backend-independent tools: GPU-to-CPU fallback, result caching, hull post-processing (hull count and vertex limits, margins), convex hulls, mass properties, mesh checks and OBJ I/O.

.NET bindings for V-HACD 4 (Voxelized Hierarchical Approximate Convex Decomposition), the decomposition behind many game engine and physics toolchains. Fast and voxel-based; runs on the CPU with no extra runtime dependencies.

.NET bindings for CoACD (Approximate Convex Decomposition for 3D Meshes with Collision-Aware Concavity and Tree Search, SIGGRAPH 2022). Built from source with an exception-safe native shim; runs on the CPU with no extra runtime dependencies.

.NET bindings for CuACD, a fully GPU-resident approximate convex decomposition (ACD) of 3D meshes. A CUDA-accelerated alternative to CoACD, typically 50-100x faster. Requires an NVIDIA GPU and driver; no CUDA toolkit needed.
